answer: The thread multiplier is published, charged in prism, and island lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 9 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 3694 identities would post 1043 proofs and burn roughly 26 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
